findings.summary: On a marketing site, every page except the home opens on a compact product header band: a title-size heading, one sticker, no actions. Plan prices are 18px flags inside cards. The reference treats its own pricing and features pages as posters. Each gets a full band hero with a display headline and several cropped stickers around it. On pricing, a black seam then closes that hero into a split band where each half holds one huge fee figure. So the page that sells the product, and its states, lose the system's loudest moment and read like a settings page.
findings.promptFix: On a marketing site, every top-level page (pricing, features, about, customers), not only the home, opens on a hero band, never a compact header band. Give it an eyebrow, a font.size.display–font.size.hero headline, a lead and 3–6 stickers cropped at the side edges, in a band colour other than the home hero's. On a pricing page, close that hero with a 1px ink seam into a split band, one half per plan or fee, with its figure set at font.size.display, before any card grid or comparison table. Compact header bands are for product, form, docs and settings screens.

findings.summary: Below the hero, the marketing home slips into generic SaaS sections on plain paper. There is a six-up grid of small icon cards with ~12px grey copy, a boxed stat strip and three small quote cards, and the pink closing band carries a default-size button. The reference keeps every section weighty: large titles, split colour bands and process ribbons carrying stickers, and a closing action at full CTA size.

Sticker craft is uneven at the margins. The docs hero ring is about 130–150px against 01's 200–260px coins, and its lower pair sit small in the corners. On a phone, the marketing hero shows only two stickers, both in the top corners, with none near the headline. Two band stickers copy the spec's example disc and stand for nothing in the product, and one band's ticket is cropped past half until it reads as a thin slab. The marquee is plain names with dots, where 12 alternates tag pills with small coloured sticker icons. The reference's stickers are large, nameable objects placed around the headline.

A header band with a sticker grows to fit the sticker instead of its content. On the overview page that leaves about 120px of empty lemon under a one-line lead. Reference 06 closes its band soon after its controls, and the content-led bands on the other docs pages already read better.
findings.promptFix: Size a header band from its content plus space.6–space.8 padding, never from its sticker. Fit the sticker to the band's content height, and let the seam crop it rather than growing the band.
findings.specRule: .ft-band--with-sticker { --ft-s: clamp(var(--size-sticker-sm), 14vw, var(--size-sticker-band)); overflow: hidden; min-height: calc(var(--ft-s) + var(--space-6) * 2);

findings.summary: In the docs header, the trailing action is a plain hairline cell, white in light and dark grey in dark. 01 and 11 make it a solid full-height block, black and then pink, that anchors the header's end. The marketing site gets this right, so the two apps' headers differ. The search clear glyph is navy, a colour outside the ink palette. Both were noted in rc.4 and remain open.

In dark mode, colour bands run straight into the black body with no seam, and panel and field outlines fade to grey. 11 keeps every field and control edge crisp. This was the same dark-mode softness as rc.4 and is still open on new products.

Dense content loses the reference's calm. Docs option tables give their type and default columns wide air and squeeze the description into wraps of 3–4 lines. On phones, the filter chip row wraps into three loose rows with one chip alone, and the page-contents list opens in full above the content. References 07, 08 and 10 keep rows even and controls in one tight row.

The signup success state uses the right word badge, but the badge is small in its panel, and the next step is a default-size button with no plate stack. The reference gives a screen's main next action clear weight.

Docs on a phone: the hero lead and its stacked actions run flush to the screen edges with no gutter. The top bar breaks into two rows with a lopsided half-height link cell instead of moving the links into the menu. The brand's focus ring hugs the wordmark with no offset.
On phones, comparison and option tables cut their columns at the frame. There is no sticky first column, no scroll cue and no stacked fallback, so later plan columns and descriptions are hidden.

notes: Review: 75/75 checklist items by 4 reviewer(s) and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/felt-tip-market/0.1.0-rc.4/review-3-holdout).

The language carries to both new products. Each hero has a lemon band, a 96px headline, a black CTA beside an outline button, and thick ink-outlined stickers on their own subject cropped at the edges. The dark inversion matches 11 (pink CTA, unchanged bands), and a careful eye would take the home screens for the reference team's work. The docs chrome (compact bands, ink-framed code, pill tabs, dashed empty states) is close to 06/07.

The gap from the reference is poster ambition beyond the home hero. The marketing pricing and customers pages open on compact product bands, and the home's middle sections fall back to generic icon-card and stat-strip forms. Pricing is where 02 is loudest, so the selling page reads as a settings page.

Craft is good but not yet the reference's: the sticker ring is light in places, dark-mode edges are soft, phone header and table handling is crude, and dense tables are unevenly proportioned. One spec rule (band min-height from sticker size) directly causes empty band space.
